reports.title: DYCOM INDUSTRIES, INC. REPORTS FISCAL 2027 THIRD QUARTER RESULTS

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: Based on strong third quarter results and expectations for the remainder of the year, the Company is updating its outlook:

Contract revenues | $7.66 billion to $7.73 billion
Communications | $6.00 billion to $6.04 billion
Building Systems | $1.66 billion to $1.69 billion

The Company is maintaining its fiscal 2027 outlook for consolidated Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA margin that is expected to increase compared to the prior year, comprised of strong margins in the Building Systems segment partially offset by a decline in Communications margins from cost pressures to scale operations and from higher fuel costs.
For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, the Company currently expects the following:

Contract revenues | $1.63 billion to $1.70 billion
Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA | $204 million to $218 million
Non-GAAP Adjusted Diluted EPS (excluding amortization expense) | $2.48 to $2.78

For additional information regarding the Company’s outlook, please see the “Outlook Expectations Summary” available on the Company’s Investor Center website posted in connection with the conference call discussed below.

desk.headline: Revenue up 41.6% to $2.06bn and adjusted EPS of $5.23, both above estimates; record $12.9bn backlog and full-year revenue outlook raised
results: Revenue rose 41.6% to $2.06bn (11.2% organic), helped by the acquired Building Systems business; adjusted EPS rose 33% to $5.23, above the $4.59 estimate.
GAAP EPS fell to $3.19 from $3.63 because of much higher amortisation and interest costs and a $22.7m bad-debt charge ($0.57 a share) after a rural customer went bankrupt.
Communications revenue grew 11.2% to $1.61bn, but its EBITDA margin slipped to 12.8% from 15.1% on scaling costs and higher fuel.
Building Systems (data-centre electrical work) earned a 23.8% EBITDA margin on $441.7m of revenue.
Backlog hit a record $12.9bn (+57%); cash flow was weak, with free cash flow of -$33m, and Dycom spent $100.5m on buybacks.

guidance.summary: Full-year revenue outlook raised to $7.66–7.73bn, about $125m above the earlier midpoint, and the company still expects a higher full-year EBITDA margin. Q4 guidance reflects a 13-week quarter versus 14 weeks last year and normal winter seasonality.

points: Long-haul and data-centre link contracts more than doubled since Q2 to over $2bn, and management expects them to lead Communications growth next year.
Fibre-to-the-home work was up about 50% so far this year but is expected to fall in fiscal 2028, while staying above fiscal 2026 levels.
Early fiscal 2028 view: Communications revenue up mid-single digits with better margins; Building Systems growth in the high teens or better.
Fuel cost about 0.5 points of Communications margin; management is building fuel into renewed contracts.
Receivable days rose to 112, blamed on customer consolidation and timing; management expects several hundred million dollars of Q4 operating cash flow and added a $200m buyback authorisation.
call.source: Presentation slides (Exhibit 99.2); call coverage: The Motley Fool transcript, 24 Nov 2026; Investing.com, 24 Nov 2026

watch: Whether receivable days come down and Q4 cash flow arrives as promised.
Communications margins as fuel and scaling costs persist.
How fast long-haul, data-centre and copper-reclamation work offsets the expected fibre-to-the-home slowdown in fiscal 2028.
